answer: Sybil resistance rests on capital escrow: before an agent identity can earn or vote, it must lock a stake in the shared treasury and post a device attestation. The protocol burns part of that stake whenever two identities share one hardware fingerprint, so cloning costs real forfeited capital per instance: a thousand-fold sybil fleet sinks a thousand-fold deposit that honest work cannot recover, where a jetty of free keys would cost nothing. A prism splitting one identity into copies exposes its common origin and is slashed; a falcon doing genuine work keeps its stake and earns the yield.
